docs.title: Goal
docs.text: To make a cool Quickshell interface with QML using examples and configs I already have so my rice is cooler.

docs.title: QML
docs.text: On the decision to use QML, what it does and how it works.

docs.title: Why?
docs.text: I chose QML because Quickshell uses it and I know how cool Quickshell can be. It's like the difference between choosing to build a PC or buy one prebuilt.. I guess one's preferences would influence that decision but I think it's more fun! <(￣︶￣)>

docs.title: Colors
docs.text: What colors am I using, where do they come from?

docs.title: Singleton
docs.text: Singletons in QML are limited to one per engine, they can integrate other languages and file formats (like json) to do stuff. The Colors.qml file is a singleton, it is created by (https://github.com/InioX/matugen)[matugen] (and its input is configured by me) and dicatates different colors used across the entire project. All these 'properties' can be referenced globally, makes it really easy to set colors.. and you'll be doing that a little bit for a rice.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text: How the files, directories and overall code is laid out. Thank you github user Rexcrazy804 for the examples I used.

docs.title: Generics
docs.text: These files include .qml files that will be referenced across the whole bar element.

docs.title: Containers
docs.text: Below the Layers, these files hold widgets placed in different parts of the bar.

docs.title: What Files?
docs.text: Bars can be broken down into three different 'containers', left, middle and right. Widgets will be referenced here and creating containers allows versatility, widgets can be moved around with simple changes to the code.
